data.body:
Retracting the root cause this ticket was filed with. It was wrong, and the title asserting it has been corrected.

**What was claimed:** that rebar's store push scrubs ambient `GIT_CONFIG_*` for hermeticity and thereby discards the only credential configuration, leaving the child git with no way to authenticate.

**Why that is false.** There is no scrub on the push path. `src/rebar/_store/push.py:242` builds the push environment as `push_env = {**os.environ, "PRE_COMMIT_ALLOW_NO_CONFIG": "1"}` — the full ambient environment plus one unrelated variable. It reaches git through `_git` -> `run_git_bounded` -> `run_git` (`src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py:85`), which passes `env` straight to `subprocess.run` and adds nothing. A grep across `src/rebar` for `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`, `GIT_ASKPASS`, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT` and `credential.` finds no scrub in any store write path; the only `scrub_ambient_git_config` call is in `tests/conftest.py`, which does not run in production. The scrub I attributed the failure to does not exist.

**What the environment actually looks like.** The orchestrator shell does carry the injected configuration I described: `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=8` with `credential.interactive = 'never'` at index 1 and `credential.helper = ''` at index 5, plus `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`. `git config --get credential.interactive` returns `never`. That part of the observation stands.

**But that configuration does not prevent authentication.** Tested directly from the tracker, against the same `origin` (`https://github.com/navapbc/rebar.git`) that rebar pushes to, forcing a real authenticated round-trip rather than a no-op:

- with the ambient configuration exactly as-is: `git push --dry-run origin HEAD:refs/heads/tmp-cred-probe-<pid>` -> `* [new branch]`, success.
- with every `GIT_CONFIG_*` variable unset, which is what the hypothesised scrub would have produced: same command -> `* [new branch]`, success.

Both authenticate. So neither the ambient prohibition nor its removal explains the failure. (Note an earlier attempt at this test returned `Everything up-to-date` and proved nothing — git short-circuits before contacting the remote when there is nothing to push. The probe ref was a dry run and was confirmed absent from the remote afterwards.)

**A discriminator did emerge.** Writes routed through the configured MCP server push successfully: closing `psychotic-selfless-ragfish` returned `"push_status":{"state":"ok"}`, and the edit that corrected this ticket's title likewise returned `state: ok`. Writes from the local CLI in this shell fail. Same repository, same remote, same tracker.

**So the failure is real and reproducible but currently unexplained.** It has occurred on every local CLI write attempted in this session — at least seven times, including during the creation of this ticket — always as `WARNING rebar._store.push_classify: tickets branch push failed (exit 128): fatal: unable to get password from user`, always with the local write itself succeeding and the branch silently not publishing. Each failure also records a `push-pending` sentinel that then wedges the gates, which remains `abnormal-dear-shoveler` (`16c9-a42d-fd01-48b9`) and is unaffected by this retraction.

**What a next investigation should establish**, rather than assume: what differs between the git invocation rebar makes and the by-hand invocation that succeeds, given that the environment and the remote are shared. Candidates worth eliminating in order - whether the CLI process reaches this code with an environment differing from its own shell's (something between the entry point and the push mutating `os.environ`), whether `capture_output=True` changes credential-helper behaviour by denying git a usable stdio channel, and whether the failing pushes are specifically those that take the non-fast-forward recovery path rather than the direct push. The first of these is cheap to settle by having the push path log the credential-relevant keys it is about to hand to git.

The acceptance criteria are left as written: they describe the behaviour required of a fix and do not depend on the retracted mechanism. AC2's wording about preserving the scrub's hermeticity property should be re-read once the real cause is known, since it presumes a scrub that is not there.
